articles.title: 'Hand of unity' vs 'unhinged incitement': Likud, Eisenkot trade barbs over Netanyahu's offer
articles.summary: Israel's ruling Likud Party has accused opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot of making inflammatory remarks against caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.body: Israel's ruling Likud Party has accused opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot of making inflammatory remarks against caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his office, describing his statements as "unhinged incitement".The party also questioned allegations surrounding Netanyahu's chief of staff.In a post on X, Likud criticised Eisenkot for making provocative remarks despite Netanyahu's invitation to join hands and form a national unity government."Gadi Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement against Prime Minister Netanyahu and his office is appalling. While the prime minister extends a hand of unity, Eisenkot and his colleagues issue inflammatory, incendiary statements every day in venomous language," the party said.Defending Netanyahu's chief of staff, Likud said the official had fulfilled his obligations by informing the police about suspected serious criminal activity."Eisenkot is inciting against the chief of staff, a law-abiding citizen who passed information to the police about suspected serious criminal activity, as he was obligated to do," the party said.The ruling party also questioned the allegations against the official, asking, "Did the chief of staff plant the envelopes of cash with the suspects? The absurdity of Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement is outrageous."The exchange comes amid growing political tensions between Netanyahu and Eisenkot over the formation of Israel's next government and allegations linked to the Prime Minister's Office.Netanyahu had earlier invited Eisenkot to hold negotiations without preconditions to form a national unity government, arguing that Israel needed a broad political coalition to tackle its security challenges, particularly the threat from Iran.In a video statement, Netanyahu said his recent conversation with Eisenkot had strengthened his belief in the need for a broad-based government. He argued that a narrow coalition, or one dependent on parties he described as supporters of terrorism, would be unable to address the country's security challenges.Netanyahu also urged political leaders to set aside their differences and proposed resolving the issue of military conscription through discussions involving representatives of the Haredi community.However, Eisenkot, who leads the Yashar party, rejected the proposal, calling Netanyahu's overture "another spin". He said negotiating teams from Likud and Yesh Atid had already scheduled a meeting.Eisenkot also maintained that any national emergency government formed under his leadership would have to accept his proposed principles and break away from extremist political forces.The political standoff follows last month's election, in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority. Israeli President Isaac Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate to form a government last week.Meanwhile, finance minister and Religious Zionism Party chairman Bezalel Smotrich backed Netanyahu's appeal for unity, urging Eisenkot to accept the proposal and describing it as an opportunity to demonstrate national responsibility.You use AI every day. articles.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial in March 2027 over murder of three children
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of strangling her three children to death in January 2023, will face a second trial on March 29, 2027,
articles.body: Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of strangling her three children to death in January 2023, will face a second trial on March 29, 2027, after her first trial ended in a mistrial earlier this year.According to the New York Post, prosecutors from Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz’s office said on Monday that they were prepared to proceed with a jury trial against the 36-year-old, although they did not explicitly confirm whether they would pursue the same first-degree murder charges.Clancy’s defence lawyer, Kevin Reddington, said he understood the prosecution's position to mean that it intended to proceed with the first-degree murder indictments she faced in the previous trial.“I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it’s an indirect comment from the DA that they intend to proceed on first-degree indictments, so we will pick a trial date,” Reddington said.Judge William Sullivan set March 29 as the trial date, overriding the prosecution's objection. Prosecutors had sought to push the proceedings until May, citing scheduling conflicts.The first trial, which lasted several weeks over the summer, ended in September after the 12-member jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. The BBC reported that the mistrial followed a deadlock over the charges.A week before the latest hearing, Sullivan rejected a defence bid to dismiss the case on double jeopardy grounds, clearing the way for prosecutors to bring Clancy to trial again.Clancy is accused of killing her three children on January 24, 2023. She does not deny killing them, but her defence team argues that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors maintain that the killings were intentional.She is currently being held at a state-run psychiatric hospital in Massachusetts. Her lawyer had previously indicated that he would consider a plea deal if prosecutors agreed that she could remain in psychiatric care rather than be sent to prison.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oprah Winfrey packed a care bag and wrote a personal note for a woman she may never meet, joining an Australian charity drive that has collected over 1.1 million bags and now hopes to gather 150,000 more
articles.summary: A parcel sent from the United States has become part of an Australian Christmas charity campaign after television host Oprah Winfrey packed a care bag for
articles.body: A parcel sent from the United States has become part of an Australian Christmas charity campaign after television host Oprah Winfrey packed a care bag for a stranger and included a handwritten note. According to a media release from Bunnings Australia, Winfrey took part in Share the Dignity's annual It's in the Bag appeal, which runs across Australia from 6 to 22 November 2026. The campaign encourages people to fill a new or pre-loved handbag, backpack or tote with everyday essentials, period products and a personal message. The packed bags can then be dropped off at a local Bunnings store. The campaign supports women and girls facing homelessness, domestic violence and financial hardship. This year, the charity hopes to collect 150,000 bags to meet growing demand from its registered charity partners.A personal note from across the PacificShare the Dignity Founder and Managing Director Rochelle Courtenay invited Winfrey to join the campaign after meeting her at an event in Australia and explaining the charity's work. Winfrey later packed a bag in the United States and sent it to Australia. She also included a handwritten 'Dear Her' note for the woman who would eventually receive it. "I'll admit I let out a squeal when the bag arrived," Courtenay said in the Bunnings release. "But what stays with me is the note. Oprah has written to a woman she will probably never meet. That is what Australians have been doing for eleven years: one woman saying to another, I don't know you, but I thought of you."Courtenay explained that Winfrey's donation would be distributed in exactly the same way as every other bag collected through the campaign. "Oprah's bag will do what every other bag does. It will go to one woman who needs it. It carries the same message as a bag packed by a grandmother in Toowoomba or a family in Darwin: you are seen, you matter, someone cares," Courtenay stated.Ten years of community collectionsNovember 2026 marks 10 years since Share the Dignity partnered with hardware retailer Bunnings to provide collection points across Australia. During this period, Australians have donated more than 1.1 million bags through the campaign. In 2025, people handed in 123,295 bags at physical collection points. Online donations also helped pay for more than 30,000 additional bags. "You don't have to register or attend an event," Courtenay said. "You can simply pack a bag, take it to Bunnings, and we get it into the hands of someone who needs it."Melissa O'Neill, Bunnings Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, said in the company's announcement that employees, customers and local communities had supported the campaign for a decade. "For 10 years, our team members, customers and communities have embraced Share the Dignity's It's in the Bag appeal, helping provide essential items and a message of care to women and girls experiencing homelessness, domestic violence or financial hardship," O'Neill said. "Every bag represents a simple act of kindness that can make a meaningful difference to someone at a difficult time, which is why this appeal continues to resonate so strongly with our teams and customers."She encouraged people to visit participating stores and donate before the campaign ends on 22 November. "We encourage anyone who can, to pack a bag and drop it into a participating Bunnings store between 6 and 22 November, helping remind someone they're not alone this Christmas," O'Neill added.Rising demand and lived experienceThe target of 150,000 bags comes as support services across Australia face growing demand. Figures from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, cited by Bunnings, show that nearly 289,000 people received support from specialist homelessness services across the country in 2024-25. Of these, 17,063 women and children affected by family violence experienced ongoing homelessness. This was higher than the 15,510 recorded in 2022-23.For people receiving the donations, the bags can provide practical help during some of the most difficult periods of their lives. One recipient, Lenna Boxall, received a donated bag while undergoing treatment for breast cancer, major surgery, chronic pain and medical menopause. At the same time, she was caring for her three daughters and two nieces, whose mother had fled domestic violence. "It was a really, really big, incredible thing at the time, receiving a bag. It just made me feel seen and cared about. I just really appreciated that people cared enough to want to help," Boxall said in the release. "I'm strong and I'm tough, but I'm also human and I'm an emotional person and I feel a lot... I'm learning it's ok for me to accept help."How the public can take partCourtenay founded Share the Dignity in 2015 after learning that women experiencing homelessness were sometimes unable to afford basic sanitary products during their periods. Since then, the charity has grown with the support of more than 2,500 volunteers across Australia and has distributed over six million packets of period products. "We don't need 150,000 Oprahs," Courtenay said. "We need 150,000 Australians willing to care about someone they may never meet. Find a handbag, backpack or tote you no longer use. Fill it with the essentials, add something lovely, and write a Dear Her note. That note may be the most important thing you put inside." People can drop off their completed bags at participating Bunnings stores until 22 November 2026. Those who cannot visit a store can also support the campaign by funding a bag online through Share the Dignity's website.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US tightens AI chip curbs: How Trump plans to block China's indirect access to American technology
articles.summary: The Trump administration has introduced new export control rules to prevent China and other restricted countries from gaining indirect access to advanced
articles.body: The Trump administration has introduced new export control rules to prevent China and other restricted countries from gaining indirect access to advanced American artificial intelligence (AI) chips and computing power through overseas data centres.The rules, announced by the US Commerce Department on Monday, seek to close loopholes that allow Chinese companies to rent computing capacity powered by American technology from facilities located in third countries. The restrictions took effect immediately.The move comes amid growing concerns in Washington that existing export controls are insufficient to prevent China from accessing advanced US chips through cloud computing services and data centres in Southeast Asia.“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries,” the Bureau of Industry and Security under the Commerce Department said while announcing the new restrictions.Under the rules, overseas data centres providing services to companies in countries including China, Russia, Iran and Cuba will be required to identify their end users. Additional licensing requirements will also apply to chip sales involving Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which the rules identify as countries that “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" to unauthorised destinations.Why is the US tightening AI chip restrictions?The US has imposed restrictions on exports of its most advanced AI chips to China to maintain its technological advantage in the global artificial intelligence race.However, American lawmakers and policymakers have raised concerns that Chinese companies could bypass these restrictions by accessing computing power remotely through cloud services.Under existing rules, restrictions primarily focus on the physical export of advanced chips. This has created concerns that companies in restricted countries could rent processing capacity from data centres located in countries where American chips can be legally deployed.Last year, US Representative Michael Lawler, a Republican from New York, introduced legislation seeking to expand export controls to cover remote access to advanced computing technology.He told Congress that “physical export controls” under existing rules do not cover remote access, allowing China to “access our tech through the cloud” and giving it “a real tool to sidestep” US export restrictions.The bill has passed the House of Representatives, while lawmakers in the Senate are also pursuing measures to tighten restrictions.These proposals include allowing Congress to review licences for advanced AI chip sales to China, requiring the Commerce Department to track chips to prevent their diversion to unauthorised destinations, and pushing US allies such as the Netherlands and Japan to align their export restrictions with Washington.Megaspeed controversy puts export controls under scrutinyThe latest restrictions come amid scrutiny of Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US export controls.The company provides computing power to Chinese businesses using chips installed in data centres across Southeast Asia, including facilities in Malaysia.Last week, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faced criticism after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Commerce Department had been late in imposing restrictions on Nvidia chip exports linked to Megaspeed.President Donald Trump acknowledged tensions between the Treasury and Commerce departments over the issue on Monday. He suggested Lutnick may have delayed imposing restrictions to avoid a “blow up” in the fragile US-China relationship.“We’re having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, Trump said.The controversy has also drawn attention to the role of Southeast Asian countries in the supply chain for advanced AI computing infrastructure.Singapore confirmed last week that it had investigated Megaspeed over “potential false declarations" involving servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia that might have “subsequently been routed from Malaysia to another destination, contrary to declaration made in Singapore.”Malaysia has also launched an investigation into whether chips imported into the country were subsequently re-exported to other destinations in violation of applicable restrictions.“Malaysia welcomes investment in data centers and technology, but will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls,” read the Friday statement by Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry.Trump heads to Asia amid fragile trade truceThe new restrictions were announced on the same day Trump departed for an Asian tour, during which he is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping for the third time this year.The meeting comes as Washington and Beijing attempt to maintain a fragile trade truce amid continuing tensions over technology, tariffs and access to critical supply chains.The latest rules underline Washington's efforts to prevent China from accessing advanced American computing technology, even through third-country data centres, as competition between the two countries over artificial intelligence intensifies.You use AI every day. articles.title: PM to kickstart redevelopment of gurdwara in Manila
articles.summary: New Delhi: PM Narendra Modi will lay the foundation stone for major redevelopment of a historic gurdwara in Manila in Philippines Tuesday, continuing his
articles.body: New Delhi: PM Narendra Modi will lay the foundation stone for major redevelopment of a historic gurdwara in Manila in Philippines Tuesday, continuing his long association with the promotion of Sikh culture and heritage in India and abroad.Officials said the ambitious and comprehensive redevelopment of Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara will make it a five-storey complex with adequate space and facilities for the community."Tomorrow, Nov 17, is a very special day. This gurdwara is over a century old and is a centre of immense spiritual significance. Inspired by the teachings of the Guru Sahibs, the Sikh community has made a mark globally, being at the forefront of serving others and building a better planet," Modi said on X.You use AI every day. articles.title: Michael J. Fox founded his Parkinson's research charity in 2000; its November 14 gala raised $6 million, while the foundation has directed more than $2.5 billion toward research over 25 years
articles.summary: Michael J. Fox's Parkinson's research charity gala raised a record $6 million, continuing a 25-year legacy of funding over $2.5 billion for Parkinson's research. Discover the impact and future goals of The Michael J. Fox Foundation.
articles.body: A fundraising event for Parkinson's research brought together actor Michael J. Fox, his wife and their three daughters in New York on November 14. The annual gathering marked another milestone for an organisation that the actor established after receiving his own Parkinson's diagnosis. According to USA TODAY, the event reportedly raised a record $6 million, adding to the foundation's efforts to support scientific research, improve treatments and work towards finding a cure for the neurological condition.According to The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research's official website, the organisation has deployed more than $2.5 billion towards research during its first 25 years. Founded in 2000, the charity has become the world's largest nonprofit funder of Parkinson's research. Its latest fundraising event, titled 'A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Cure Parkinson's', took place at the Waldorf Astoria in New York and brought together entertainers, supporters and members of Fox's family.Michael J. Fox attended gala with wife and daughtersFox, 65, attended the November 14 event with his wife, Tracy Pollan, and their three daughters, Esmé, 25, and twins Aquinnah and Schuyler, 31. Their appearance together attracted attention, as the family rarely makes public appearances as a group. The couple also have a son, Sam, 37, who was not present at the event. According to USA TODAY's report, the fundraiser featured musical performances by John Mayer and Brad Paisley, comedy appearances and several celebrity guests. Comedian Denis Leary hosted the evening, while performers and supporters came together to raise money for Parkinson's research.The event also featured a performance involving Fox, Mayer, members of Super Soul Banned and No Doubt guitarist Tom Dumont, who had publicly shared his early-onset Parkinson's diagnosis earlier in 2026. The gala was particularly significant for Fox and Pollan, who have spent decades supporting research into the condition. Speaking to PEOPLE at the event, Pollan said the money raised goes towards supporting scientists and their work. She also described the progress made through the foundation's long-running efforts.Fox established foundation after Parkinson's diagnosisFox was diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson's disease in 1991, when he was 29 years old. The actor initially kept his diagnosis private before publicly disclosing it in 1998. Two years after publicly disclosing his diagnosis, he established The Michael J. Fox Foundation in 2000 to accelerate research and improve the lives of people living with the condition.Parkinson's is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement. It develops when nerve cells responsible for producing dopamine, a chemical involved in controlling movement, become damaged or die. Common symptoms include tremors, muscle stiffness, slowed movement and difficulties with balance and coordination.Through his foundation, Fox sought to bring greater attention and funding to a condition that affects millions of people worldwide. The organisation supports research into the causes of Parkinson's, potential treatments, early detection and approaches that could eventually lead to a cure.Foundation reports more than $2.5 billion in research fundingThe foundation's official 'Your Gift Powers Progress' update highlights the scale of its work over the past 25 years. It states that the organisation has deployed more than $2.5 billion towards Parkinson's research since its establishment in 2000.The foundation also reports that treatment options have increased by 200 per cent since its launch, while nearly two dozen treatments have been approved over the past decade. Its work brings together researchers, medical professionals, pharmaceutical companies and people living with Parkinson's. The organisation also supports clinical studies and makes research resources available to encourage collaboration and accelerate scientific progress. For 2026, the foundation said it aimed to fund $600 million in research, reflecting its continued commitment to advancing discoveries and improving treatment options.The November 14 gala marked the 26th year of the fundraising tradition. For Fox, the event represented more than a celebrity gathering or an annual fundraising milestone. It reflected the continuing efforts of researchers, donors, families and people living with Parkinson's to move closer to better treatments and, ultimately, a cure.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Michigan man sued his brother and sister-in-law over alleged irregularities in their mother's estate; his lawsuit was dismissed and a November 13 appeals court upheld $11,000 in fees awarded against him
articles.summary: A Michigan family feud over an inheritance has become costly, after a son who questioned how his brother handled their late mother’s finances was ordered
articles.body: A Michigan family feud over an inheritance has become costly, after a son who questioned how his brother handled their late mother’s finances was ordered to pay $11,000 in legal fees. The Michigan Court of Appeals has now upheld the award, deciding that while parts of the lawsuit had questionable legal merit, the original allegations were not entirely without foundation. The November 13, 2026 ruling is an example of how disputes over the administration of an estate can result in protracted legal battles and significant financial costs whether or not claims are ultimately brought to trial.An unequal inheritance sparks a family disputeThe case concerned Frieda Mae Chapman, who died in November 2021, after the death of her husband Leonard Chapman in April 2017. The Michigan Court of Appeals said Frieda had three sons, Glenn Chapman, who received 20% of her estate; Kurt Chapman, who received 37%; and Christopher Chapman, who received 40%.Christopher had handled much of his mother’s finances in the last few years of her life, acting as trustee of her trust and having power of attorney. Glenn then asked how those duties had been fulfilled, and filed probate proceedings concerning both his mother’s estate and trust.Allegations over family money handlingThe fight continued in October 2023 when Glenn filed a separate civil suit against Christopher and his wife, Jaime Chapman. Glenn claimed his brother had abused his position of financial authority to derive personal benefits from Frieda’s money, according to Michigan Court of Appeals records.The lawsuit alleged eight claims, including breach of fiduciary duty, embezzlement, conversion, undue influence, conspiracy, unjust enrichment, quantum meruit and fraud.Christopher and Jaime denied the allegations and sought to dismiss the proceedings. The trial court first disposed of two claims and afforded Glenn the chance to amend his complaint. But the litigation continued with more motions and discovery disputes.Finally, in January 2025, Glenn moved to dismiss the case with prejudice, claiming he lacked the funds to pay his attorneys.Lawyer fees battlegroundChristopher and Jaime sought a large legal fee after Glenn dropped the suit. Christopher wanted $37,352.10, Jaime $46,467.50. Their requests increased to $41,772.10 and $47,922.50.In May 2025, the probate court dismissed the complaint and ordered each defendant to pay $5,500 in attorney fees and costs, totaling $11,000.The Michigan Court of Appeals noted that the lower court did not find the lawsuit to be frivolous in its entirety, nor did it find that it was filed primarily to harass or injure the defendants. It did, however, find that Glenn should have realized earlier that the litigation was getting off on the wrong foot.Appeals court denies request for higher paymentsChristopher and Jaime appealed the $11,000 award, saying the original complaint was frivolous and they should be reimbursed for their entire legal bill.But the Michigan Court of Appeals saw it differently. The appellate panel, in its Nov. 13 decision, said the lower court did not clearly err in concluding the lawsuit was not frivolous when it was filed.The court recognized that certain claims were legally quite weak, especially those concerning embezzlement and conversion. It also found some of the allegations against Jaime were less compelling because she was not in a formal fiduciary position over Frieda’s finances.But the judges found the main allegation about Christopher’s fiduciary duties to be reasonable. The proceedings heard evidence including financial records which showed that money from accounts associated with Frieda and her late husband had been used for some personal expenses.The Michigan Court of Appeals also considered the likelihood that Christopher had used his position of trust to influence financial decisions that affected his mother. It said that these facts gave Glenn sufficient reason to proceed with the main accusations even if the allegations were never litigated.The $11,000 prize standsIn dismissing the appeal, the Michigan Court of Appeals drew a distinction between a lawsuit that fails and one that is legally frivolous. Michigan law provides that a claim may be deemed frivolous if it is filed primarily to harass someone, if there is no reasonable factual basis for the claim, or if the claim lacks any arguable legal merit.But the appellate judges found that the original lawsuit as a whole didn’t rise to that level. But they also found no reason to overturn the trial court's decision to award $11,000 for legal expenses incurred in the later stages of the legal proceedings.The Nov. 13 ruling keeps the original fee awards in place. Christopher and Jaime keep their original $5,500 awards against Glenn.The ruling does not settle whether Christopher mishandled his mother’s finances or resolve the underlying allegations of financial wrongdoing. However, it does not address the legal basis for the award of fees, and it further supports the distinction between unsuccessful litigation and proceedings that meet the frivolous standard under Michigan law.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day.
